title: Pre-A1 phonics distillation (Letters and Sounds–style)
attribution: Distilled pedagogical structure oriented by Letters and Sounds (DfES-00281-2007, Crown copyright 2007). See SOURCES.md. Lang-Tutor rewrite — not a PDF republication.

sections.title: Early phonics ladder overview
sections.body: Pre-A1 uses a gentle phase ladder: (1) oral sound awareness and blending without letters; (2) first simple GPCs with short practice words; (3) remaining single letters and a few common digraphs only when ready; (4) adjacent consonants (CVCC/CCVC) as a stretch, not a day-one goal. Later Letters and Sounds phases (broad alternative spellings, longer morphology) are out of scope for this chapter’s core bar.

sections.title: Phase: Oral awareness
sections.body: Environmental sounds, voice sounds, rhythm and rhyme, oral blending and segmenting of short spoken words. No letter symbols required. Goal: hear and play with sounds before mapping them to print.

sections.title: Phase: Early GPCs
sections.body: Introduce a small set of high-utility single-letter GPCs (classic early set includes letters such as s, a, t, p, i, n, m, d) with short practice words. Keep grapheme–phoneme links consistent; celebrate accurate sounding and blending of very short words.

sections.title: Phase: More letters (gentle)
sections.body: Add remaining single letters and only a few common digraphs when the learner is steady on early GPCs. Prefer accuracy and confidence over coverage speed. Do not dump full digraph charts into beginner prompts.

sections.title: Phase: Adjacent consonants (stretch)
sections.body: Optional stretch for stronger beginners: CVCC and CCVC shapes (e.g. lamp, stop). Still keep vocabulary concrete and short. Skip if the Alphabet runway or early GPCs are not yet secure.

sections.title: Out of scope for pre-A1 core
sections.body: Broad alternative vowel spellings, advanced morphology, long irregular word banks, and full handbook activity scripts from Letters and Sounds are not pre-A1 chapter goals. Point advanced literacy to later tiers.
